notes.unverified: Not verified and therefore left out: Thursday's investor flows, which Amwal Al Ghad gives in billions of pounds, so the flows chart is dropped; Thursday's breadth and turnover; a second source for Thursday's index closes (only Amwal Al Ghad was found; the StockAnalysis closes move in line); the CBE's closing rate; Brent against the budget's oil assumption; the reserves split between foreign currency and gold. Banky's gold page shows 12 November in its header but 13 November in its body, and lists the ounce in pounds although its metadata says dollars, so the gold row shows no ounce price. Investing.com says spot gold had its worst week since March but futures their worst since early June.

items: Brent jumps 3.3% to $95.82 on Thursday after Houthi strikes on Saudi oil sites and Iran's attack on a US radar in Bahrain → renewed attacks on Gulf energy put oil back near $96, a cost for Egypt's import bill.
Gold falls to a 13-month low and is down 3.5% this week; 21K gold in Egypt drops to about EGP 5,975 a gram → markets fully price a December Fed hike, which lifts the dollar.
EGX30 falls 0.91% to 52,023 on Thursday, while Housing and Development Bank jumps 5.79% → blue chips take profits after a strong week; banks with earnings news still rise.
Suez Canal Bank's nine-month profit rises 12.9% to EGP 5.7 bn as interest income grows about 43% → high rates keep lifting bank income.

Israel's security cabinet orders the army to step up preparations for a possible attack on Iran, and Tehran threatens bases from West Asia to Europe → a renewed war would hit oil, Gulf shipping and the pound just as markets price a wind-down.
Eastern Company's nine-month profit rises 39% to about EGP 9 bn, and the stock gains 4.17% → sales rise 11% and margins widen, which supports the stock.
EGX30 ends flat at 52,500 on Wednesday after two days of gains, with turnover at EGP 11.79 bn → the rally pauses as small caps take profits; fertiliser stocks rebound.
The government targets public debt of about 69.5% of GDP by 2030 and frees a Red Sea plot to help pay it down → lower debt would ease debt-service costs over time.
EGX30 jumps 2.08% to 52,483 on Tuesday, a second day of gains, with EFG Holding up 6.75% → slower inflation and foreign buying of Egyptian T-bills lift sentiment.
Remittances rise 20.4% to a record $13 bn in July to September, and reach $38.2 bn in the first nine months of 2026 → the largest source of dollars for Egypt keeps growing despite the regional war.
Hotter US inflation and a hawkish Waller make a December Fed hike nearly certain → a higher US rate narrows the carry on Egyptian debt and lifts the cost of Egypt's floating-rate loans.
Foreign investors buy about $614.7 mn of Egyptian T-bills on Monday while selling stocks → the carry trade returns, which supports the pound.

Urban inflation slows to 12.7% in October from 13.9%, a nine-month low, while core inflation eases to 13.1% → the CBE's 20% deposit rate is now about 7.3 points above inflation (derived), giving it room to hold on 17 December.
Brent falls 5.85% on Monday and trades at $91.88 on Tuesday after Trump calls the Iran war effectively over → cheaper oil eases Egypt's fuel import bill and pressure on the pound.
EGX30 rises 1.19% to 51,415 on Monday, but foreigners net sell EGP 302.9 mn → local investors drive the gains while foreign money takes profits.
Egypt Aluminum's quarterly profit more than doubles to EGP 4.93 bn → profit grows far faster than sales, which supports the stock's valuation.

The government raises gas cuts to fertiliser and methanol plants to 33% from 20% and notifies Ezz Steel of a 30% cut, with no end date → Asian LNG prices jump about 36% in a month, so Egypt saves gas for power and defers five of 15 November cargoes.
Abu Qir Fertilizers falls 5.78% and MOPCO 5.85% on Sunday as the EGX30 slips 0.67% to 50,812 → the gas cuts hit output at Egypt's largest urea exporters just as urea prices rise.
Evergreen's Ever Eon crosses the Suez Canal on Sunday, the line's first transit in nearly three years → the return of another major carrier supports canal revenue and dollar inflows.

Brent falls 1.5% to $96.91 in Asia on Monday as Trump says new strikes on Iran are very unlikely while talks progress → a US land blockade is now in effect, but de-escalation hopes outweigh new shipping attacks.

stories.h: Trump drops the push for an Iran deal and keeps the blockade
stories.what: Trump says Washington no longer needs a deal with Iran and tells Vice President Vance to focus on domestic issues instead of the talks. Iran's top security official rules out removing its enriched nuclear material, and attacks on Saudi energy sites and tankers continue. Qatar and Turkiye sign a defence agreement. Brent settles 0.3% higher at $96.13 on Friday and WTI at $88.92, but both fall about 2% on the week.
stories.why: Analysts read the move as the US relying on the blockade and sanctions rather than new strikes. "We remain cautious on this prospect given the countless head-fakes," says Macquarie's Walt Chancellor.
stories.aff: Oil, Gulf LNG, shipping and regional risk premiums.
stories.eg: Without a deal, Egypt faces higher energy import costs and a slower Suez recovery.
stories.egx: Bearish for importers, tourism and logistics.

stories.h: European gas jumps 12% in a week; Goldman sees €150 if Gulf LNG stays cut
stories.what: The Dutch TTF benchmark rises 4.2% on Friday to €96.18/MWh, up 12% on the week, as US-Iran diplomacy collapses; EU storage is 71% full. Goldman Sachs sees TTF near €150 in the first quarter of 2027 if Persian Gulf LNG exports average 25-30% of pre-war levels and the winter is colder than normal.
stories.why: Traders fear a wider war could shut LNG routes through Hormuz.
stories.aff: Global LNG prices and import-dependent buyers such as Egypt.
stories.eg: Higher LNG prices raise the cost of any gas Egypt imports and of gas-heavy industry.
stories.egx: Bearish for fertiliser, steel and other gas-heavy industry.

key.l: spot gold, week to Friday 13 Nov

stories.h: Gold has its worst week since March; 21K falls to EGP 5,950 in Egypt
stories.what: Spot gold settles at $3,884.77 on Friday, down 4.7% on the week, as traders see a December Fed hike as certain: about 90% odds for a quarter point and 10% for a half point. The dollar index rises 1.1% on the week. In Egypt, Banky puts 21K gold at EGP 5,950 a gram and the gold pound at EGP 47,600, both down 2.7% on the day.
stories.why: Strong US jobs data, hot inflation and a hawkish Waller push up rate expectations.
stories.aff: Local gold prices and household savings.
stories.eg: Cheaper gold lowers the cost of a popular savings asset in Egypt.
stories.egx: Neutral for the EGX; a stronger dollar is a risk for the pound.

key.l: EGX30 weekly gain to Thu 12 Nov (derived)

stories.h: EGX30 ends the week up about 1.7% as banks lead
stories.what: The EGX30 closes the week at 52,023.37 on Thursday, down 0.91% on the day but about 1.7% above the previous Thursday (derived). The EGX70 ends at 18,527.43 and market cap at about EGP 4.17 tn. In the brief's table, Housing and Development Bank gains about 9.0% and QNB Egypt about 9.4% over five sessions (derived), while Abu Qir Fertilizers loses about 4.3%.
stories.why: Banks lead the gains; the sources give no single cause.
stories.eg: The rally rests on local buying and a firmer pound.
stories.egx: Bullish for banks; bearish for gas-heavy industry.
stories.names: Housing and Development Bank, QNB Egypt (up); Abu Qir Fertilizers (down).

key.l: oil wells in the EGPC-Halliburton programme

stories.h: EGPC and Halliburton plan a 50-well fracking programme over 18 months
stories.what: EGPC and Halliburton sign an agreement to prepare an 18-month programme of 50 oil wells using horizontal drilling and multi-stage fracking, witnessed by Petroleum Minister Karim Badawi. Separately, Abu Qir Fertilizers signs an EGP 76.17 mn deal with the Arab Organization for Industrialization for about 3 MW of solar plants, due within 12 months.
stories.why: The state wants more local output to cut costly fuel imports.
stories.aff: Oil output, energy imports and industrial energy costs.
stories.eg: More local production would ease the import bill over time.
stories.egx: Mildly bullish for energy-linked names; small positive for Abu Qir's energy costs.
